stories.title: Ireland men set for maiden tour of Pakistan in January, to play three ODIs
summary: The Ireland men’s team will tour Pakistan in January for the first time to play three One-day Internationals against the hosts, the cricket boards of both countries announced on Thursday.

The visitors, according to the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), are scheduled to arrive in the country on Jan 9, and will take on national developmental side Pakistan Shaheens for three warm-up one-day matches between Jan 13 and 17.

For the hosts, meanwhile, the tour would be an opportunity to test their depth – especially through the Shaheens matches – and continue the fine-tuning process of their combinations ahead of the World Cup.

stories.title: SBCA chief removed as CM Murad orders sweeping action over building collapse in Karachi's Baloch Colony
summary: He said public safety must remain the “foremost responsibility” of every government department and warned that negligence in enforcing building regulations would lead to strict action, the statement added.
Rescue workers also needed to enter the collapsed building, using sensors and vibration to find bodies before initiating debris removal operations.
On Wednesday, the now-removed East DC told Dawn it had transpired during the initial probe that the SBCA had given the approval for constructing the ground-plus-one-storey building to its owner.

stories.title: Makkah pact nations to discuss conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis in Islamabad meeting, Asif says
summary: The Makkah pact nations will discuss the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi fighters in Yemen when officials from the mutual defence agreement meet in Islamabad on Thursday, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif told AFP.

Asif said the “continuous turmoil south of Saudi Arabia will obviously be one agenda point in the meeting and it is very important”, confirming that defence and foreign ministers from the Gulf kingdom, Turkiye and Pakistan would attend.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the pact in August, with the three Muslim nations pledging to come to each other’s aid in the event of an attack.

stories.title: Security breach case: IHC seeks replies from parties on Imaan, Hadi's appeals against their conviction
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday issued notices and sought replies from parties on appeals filed by lawyers Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha against their convictions in a security breach case.
Imaan and Hadi filed appeals in the IHC against their convictions on Nov 7.
The Supreme Court directed the IHC to decide on the petition filed by the couple in the case.

stories.title: Bilawal terms PTI a ‘political reality’, calls for restoring its trust in the ‘system’
summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Thursday asserted that PTI was a “political reality” whose trust in the “system” needs to be restored for a political reset to take place.
On Nov 17, in a hard-hitting speech, Bilawal had asserted that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”.

At the same time, the PPP chairman highlighted a similar “lack of trust” in the opposition on the government’s part and urged the opposition to view its role as a responsibility rather than a choice. “They should sit in our finance committee in the Parliament.

stories.title: Local holiday announced in Islamabad, Rawalpindi on Nov 27
summary: A local holiday has been declared in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) and Rawalpindi for Nov 27 (Friday).
A notification issued by the Islamabad deputy commissioner stated that Nov 27 “has been declared a local holiday within the revenue limits of ICT”.
Separately, the Rawalpindi deputy commissioner shared a notification on X stating that a local holiday had been declared in the district for Nov 27.

stories.title: Other realms
summary: IT was a moment of pride for Pakistan when PAF officer Muhammad Zeeshan Ali blasted off into space yesterday morning alongside his Chinese colleagues, astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi.
As the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft entered orbit soon after lift-off, Wing Commander Ali became Pakistan’s first orbital astronaut, carrying with him “the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis”.
However, while a significant beginning has been made, it will be years before Pakistan can take the same strides in space technology as China.

stories.title: Govt to limit additional fuel cost charges to consumers at 83 paise per unit
summary: The Power Division, in a statement, said it has “proposed a Forward-looking Fuel Cost Adjustment (FFCA) mechanism wherein the increase … would be limited to approximately Rs0.83 per unit (inclusive of taxes) for the period October–December 2026” over the September FCA.

The statement came while the public hearing was in progress at the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) for an additional FCA of Rs2.88 per unit for electricity consumed in September and its billing in December.
The petition for higher FCA was filed by the Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) of the Power Division for all distribution companies (Discos), including K-Electric.

stories.title: Police use tear gas to disperse fresh Bangladesh garment worker protests
summary: Bangladesh police said they fired tear gas shells and used sound grenades to disperse protesting garment workers who tried ​to block a major highway on Thursday to press ‌their demand for better wages.

The fresh protest broke out a day after a six-member panel approved a 36 per cent increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, ​the smallest in four decades, despite weeks of protests and calls ​for the sum to be doubled.

Weeks of protests by garment workers have shuttered ​factories, blocked highways, damaged property and disrupted production in a sector that employs ‌more ⁠than four million people in a country of around 175m.

stories.title: JUI-F chief Maulana Fazl among nine party leaders barred from Sargodha district for 30 days
summary: LAHORE: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman is among nine party leaders barred from entering, residing or remaining in Sargodha district for 30 days, according to a notification issued by the deputy commissioner.
Meanwhile, several senior JUI-F leaders were detained in Sargodha and served notices for allegedly violating Section 144, police said.
Several local JUI-F leaders were also detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in Khushab district.

stories.title: PIA restores UK flight operations after Norse Atlantic disruption
summary: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) said on Thursday that it had restored normal flight operations to and from the United Kingdom, a day after two flights were cancelled by wet-lease partner Norse Atlantic as passengers prepared to board.
Norse Atlantic abruptly suspended operations on Wednesday, saying its financial situation was “critical” and it needed new financing to meet short-term liquidity needs and continue operating.

In October, the airline signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

stories.title: MNA among senior JUI-F leaders detained in Sargodha: police
summary: Several senior Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders were detained in Sargodha late on Wednesday, police said, prompting the party to demand their “immediate release”.

Sargodha Regional Police Officer (RPO) Sohail Sukhera told Dawn that Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri, a member of the National Assembly, Malik Awais and Maulana Amjad Khan were detained at a house in Sargodha and served notices for violating Section 144 imposed across the division.

Leaders detained under MPO in Khushab Meanwhile, several local JUI-F leaders were detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in Punjab’s Khushab district late on Wednesday, police said.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz launches ‘Mehfooz Dawa’ app to combat counterfeit and substandard medicines
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday launched the “Mehfooz Dawa” app to prevent the circulation of counterfeit and substandard medicines, calling it “a major milestone” and saying the initiative would help restore public confidence in the healthcare system.
The prime minister was speaking at the launch ceremony of the Ministry of National Health Services’ “Mehfooz Dawa” app, which was developed to track medicines.
Earlier this year, Drap had set October 1 as the cut-off date for launching the barcode system to curb the sale of counterfeit and expired medicines and eradicate black marketing.

stories.title: US clears SpaceX to launch up to 1 million orbital data-center satellites
summary: The Trump administration authorised Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Wednesday to launch up to one million satellites as part of its plan to build data centres in space, raising concerns from some experts.
Starmind’s satellites will communicate with those already in orbit as part of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet network, which will then relay the data to Earth.
However, there are numerous advantages to locating a data centre in space over building one on Earth.

stories.title: Major economies balk at new US tariffs over 'unfair' trade
summary: Major economies from China to the European Union hit out at proposed US tariffs after Washington concluded its months-long probe into alleged excess production, potentially opening a new phase in trade tensions with both allies and foes alike.

China is among those facing a 20 per cent tariff, but US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the levies were within the bounds of existing trade negotiations with Beijing. “China understands that we’re going to have some level of tariffs.

Trump’s tariffs have targeted Washington’s friends and foes alike, and are part of a push in his second term to remake global trade by forcing countries to buy US products or produce their goods in the country.

stories.title: ‘To the moon and beyond’: PM says Shenzhou-24 mission ‘living proof’ of Pak-China friendship
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday described the Shenzhou-24 mission as “living proof of the ironclad friendship” between Pakistan and China, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

On Wednesday, Wing Comm­ander Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign astronaut to board China’s Tiangong space station, marking a historic milestone in Pakistan’s space ambitions and Beijing’s efforts to expand its space diplomacy.
He described the mission as “living proof of the ironclad friendship” between Pakistan and China, adding that cooperation between the two countries had now “truly reached the stars”.

stories.title: IHC extends stay on Islamabad LG polls for two weeks
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday extended its interim order suspending local government elections in the federal capital by another two weeks and sought para-wise comments from the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP).
Justice Malik remarked that the commission would have to satisfy the court that the delimitation process had been completed in accordance with the law.
The ECP’s counsel maintained that the commission had carried out the delimitation exercise in accordance with the applicable law and issued an order on October 14 declaring the process complete.

stories.title: Rawalpindi ATC defers verdict in November 2024 protest case involving Aleema Khan until Dec 16
summary: RAWALPINDI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Rawalpindi on Thursday adjourned until December 16 the announcement of its reserved verdict in a case registered against Aleema Khan, sister of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, in connection with the November 26, 2024 protest.
The court had reserved its verdict in the case on September 22, fixing Sept 25 as the announcement date.
Aleema’s counsel had also objected to the court reserving its verdict without hearing the defence’s arguments, saying he had not been given an opportunity to present his case.

stories.title: Meta battles political storm in India as Congress party sues, stages protests
summary: India's main opposition Congress party has sued Meta and the federal government, saying that an automated content-removal system is blocking political posts and images of ​opposition leader Rahul Gandhi ahead of state elections.

Congress argues that Meta's system is blocking posts that are not "exactly identical" copies of content previously ordered removed, including birthday greetings, tributes ⁠and a wedding invitation featuring Gandhi.

"Automated tools" mandate India amended its IT rules in February to require large platforms to use technical measures "including automated tools" to find and block any post "exactly identical" to content already removed ​under a court order or a written government notice.

stories.title: Egypt says 31 dead in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns
summary: A fire erupted in Egyptian capital Cairo on Wednesday killing at least 31 people, the health ministry said, after a fuel truck reportedly overturned on a packed highway.

State media reported that the fire broke out when a truck loaded with fuel overturned on Cairo’s Ring Road — a crowded highway linking different parts of the capital — and burst into flames, engulfing nearby vehicles.
Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency.

stories.title: US chip curbs, distillation crackdown threaten Chinese AI model development, sources say
summary: China's Z.AI has fallen behind schedule on its next flagship AI model, while rival Moonshot AI expects the interval between major releases could double from six months to a year ​or longer if it loses access to overseas computing power, people familiar with the matter said.

Longer development cycles Beijing-based Moonshot is particularly exposed to the new US rule because it rents computing ‌power to ⁠train its models and prioritises overseas providers, a person with knowledge of its operations said.

As obtaining training data from Anthropic's and OpenAI's models has become increasingly difficult, Moonshot has begun distilling from models developed by Google and Meta , whose latest releases have made them attractive sources of training data, ​the person added.

stories.title: Govt declares local holiday in Islamabad, Pindi on Nov 27
summary: The government on Thursday declared a local holiday in Islamabad and Rawalpindi for November 27 without providing a reason.
An official notification stated that Friday had been "declared a local holiday within the revenue limits of Islamabad Capital Territory".
The notification added that all "essential services, including MCI, CDA, ICT Administration, Islamabad Police, IESCO, SNGPL and hospitals, will remain operational".

stories.title: Security forces kill 12 India-sponsored terrorists in multiple IBOs in Balochistan: ISPR
summary: Security forces killed 12 India-sponsored terrorists in four separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan between November 20 and 23, the military’s media wing said on Thursday.

In two separate engagements in Panjgur and Kech districts on November 22 and 23, security forces raided terrorist hideouts and killed two more terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan, the ISPR added.

Meanwhile, President Asif Ali Zardari lauded the security forces for carrying out “successful intelligence-based operations” in Balochistan against “terrorists operating under India’s patronage”, a statement issued by his office said.

stories.title: Musk pledges two SpaceX shares for every US child in $18 billion AI charm offensive
summary: The world's richest person announced the share giveaway, which is worth a total of around $18 billion, on the eve of Thanksgiving and just hours after SpaceX won US approval on Wednesday to deploy 1 million satellites for data centres in space.
In a separate post, Musk said the SpaceX company shares would be transferred next month.

SpaceX said earlier on Wednesday it would contribute one newly issued share of its Class A common stock to every currently active Trump Account, ​adding that Musk would personally match the number of shares donated by the company.

stories.title: Bilawal reiterates call for 'political reset' amid economic crisis
summary: Defining electoral reforms as a pillar of “system reset”, Bilawal urged the opposition to join the parliamentary electoral reform committee to ensure that the system is rebooted correctly.

The opposition did not weigh in on it with confidence.” Nevertheless, he said the amendment led to reforms in the judicial system, enabling equal representation from all provinces at the highest level of the judiciary.
The PPP stalwart said he was open to reforms in the current judicial system to restore their confidence.

stories.title: UK tells 100,000 strategic reservists to prepare for possible call-up, says UK, media
summary: The UK Ministry of Defence has sent letters to about 100,000 strategic reservists asking them to prepare for a possible call-up, media reported on Thursday.
For the first time since the Cold War, letters have been sent to about 100,000 strategic reservists, offering opportunities to volunteer for training and exercises, The Telegraph reported.

The reports followed a warning Tuesday from intelligence agency MI5 and the Ministry of Defence that British firms involved in supplying Ukraine’s military faced an increased risk of sabotage by Russia.

stories.title: Islamabad revises timings for government educational institutions for winter
summary: The Federal Directorate of Education (FDE) on Thursday announced revised winter timings for urban and rural educational institutions working under its ambit in Islamabad, effective from December 1, 2026, to January 29, 2027.
According to a notification issued by the FDE’s Academics Wing, single-shift institutions will operate from 8:30am to 2pm from Monday to Thursday, while on Fridays classes would end at 12:30pm.
The FDE has directed Area Education Officers and the Director (Colleges) to disseminate and implement the revised timings across institutions in their respective sectors.

stories.title: Capital Development Authority plans Blue Area-style bylaws for Islamabad Avenue
summary: The CDA board also approved naming the road “Islamabad Avenue”.

Board forms committee to frame regulations for commercial development along 3.8km road linking Park Road with Margalla Enclave Previously, the road passed through the national park and Zone III, a protected area.
Consequently, the CDA board decided to formulate new bylaws for the road, similar to those applicable to Blue Area.

stories.title: Fazlur Rehman, eight others barred from entering Sargodha for 30 days
summary: The Sargodha district administration imposed a 30-day ban on the entry of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and eight others, citing concerns over public safety and the maintenance of law and order.

Earlier, the JUI-F chief announced nationwide protests against restrictions imposed on the party's planned conference in Sargodha, alleging that party workers had been arrested and senior leaders placed under house arrest.
The JUI-F chief described the situation in Sargodha as curfew-like, alleging that police had taken complete control of the conference venue and were arresting party workers.

stories.title: KP dealers demand monthly fuel price revisions
summary: PESHAWAR: The Petroleum Dealers Association Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has rejected the daily revision of petroleum product prices and urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to introduce a monthly price adjustment mechanism instead.

Mr Afridi said frequent fluctuations in petroleum prices were causing substantial financial losses to petrol pump owners, who purchased stocks at one price but were often forced to sell them at reduced rates following subsequent price cuts, resulting in losses on existing stocks.
The association’s office-bearers claimed that Pakistan was the only country where petroleum prices were revised daily, arguing that no such practice existed elsewhere in the world.

stories.title: 25 Bajaur youth feared dead as boat capsizes near Libya
summary: The incident, which has plunged the entire district into utter grief and sorrow since it emerged on social media late Tuesday night, has yet to be officially confirmed by the Pakistani government, international media, or rescue organisations.
Javed Khan, an elder of Larkholozo area of Lowi Mamund, while speaking to Dawn, also confirmed that about 11 victims were from the region.
The incident has yet to be officially confirmed by the federal government, the Foreign Office, or any international organisation regarding its circumstances and the number of victims.

stories.title: PM inaugurates 'Mehfooz Dawa' app to help public identify substandard medicines
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday inaugurated the ‘Mehfooz Dawa’ mobile application, a digital initiative aimed at enabling citizens to verify the authenticity of medicines and protect against counterfeit and substandard drugs.

Drawing a comparison with the government’s fuel subsidy mechanism, the prime minister said that just as the subsidy process had been made simple and accessible, the app would also enable citizens to verify medicines conveniently.

Also Read: Cybersecurity key to achieving Digital Pakistan vision Speaking on the occasion, the health minister said that the initiative could help save precious human lives by empowering people to distinguish genuine medicines from counterfeit products.

stories.title: Arbab Niaz Stadium to be handed over to the PCB
summary: Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa has been working on a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) under which Arbab Niaz Cricket Stadium will be handed over to PCB.

It may be recalled that the name of Peshawar’s cricket stadium, previously renamed after former prime minister Imran Khan, has been changed back to Arbab Niaz Cricket Stadium on the directives of the K-P governor.
Following the decision, the stadium administration has also installed new signboards bearing the name Arbab Niaz Cricket Stadium at its entrances and other locations within the premises.

stories.title: Reminiscing about 1990s Karachi, Tajik ambassador pours his heart out
summary: In order to create a diplomatic staff for Tajikistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs the first brotherly country to offer to train us was the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
Shares fond memories of a vibrant city at ESUP talk “Pakistan played a crucial role in my life.

(L-R) Ambassador of Tajikistan, Sharifzoda Yousuf Toir, during his talk as ESUP Secretary Majyd Aziz and President Irfan Qureshi look on. — Photo by writer “In Saddar we also came across a big electronic market.

stories.title: Next Sindh local government elections to be held under 'amended law': CM Murad
summary: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah on Thursday said the next local government elections in the province would be held under a revised law aimed at granting elected local bodies greater financial, administrative and political autonomy.
He said Sindh’s existing law already provided local governments with greater powers than those in other provinces, but the provincial government wanted to strengthen the system further.

The provincial government had sought an appointment with the chief justice of the Sindh High Court on Thursday, but he was unavailable, Murad added. “We have asked the court to decide these cases within 15 days, whether the decision goes in our favour or against us,” he said.

stories.title: Shenzhou-24 mission 'living proof' of Pak-China ironclad friendship: PM Shehbaz
summary: The Shenzhou-24 mission was launched from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre on November 25, carrying Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to China’s space station, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).
Chinese Ambassador calls on the Prime Minister; PM felicitates China on historic Shenzhou-24 mission carrying Pakistan’s first astronaut.

The prime minister asked the Chinese ambassador to convey his greetings and best wishes to President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang, while paying tribute to Xi’s leadership and vision for China’s advancements in science, technology and space exploration.

stories.title: Student shot in foot as rival groups clash at Sindh University
summary: HYDERABAD: A third-year commerce student received bullet injuries to his foot at Sindh University (SU) on Wednesday during a clash between two groups of students.
The injured student was taken to Liaquat University Hospital.
According to an SU spokesman, the VC has advised students to focus on their studies and said disciplinary action would be taken accordingly.

stories.title: Sindh CM inaugurates Siemens training academy at Karachi's NED University
summary: The academy, established through a partnership between Siemens Pakistan and NED University, is the first of its kind at an engineering university and joins the company’s global network of 29 power academies across 28 countries.

It will provide specialised technical training and certification for customers and industry professionals, while giving students access to practical, industry-relevant learning and Siemens technology during their university education.

Paul Fairweather, MD of the Electrification and Automation Business Unit at Siemens Middle East, said, “What makes Pakistan unique is that we are taking a global Siemens training model into a university for the first time.

stories.title: James becomes oldest with NBA triple-double in Sixers win
summary: LeBron James became the oldest player in NBA history to produce a triple-double, leading Philadelphia to a 114-104 victory over Miami in the NBA Cup on Wednesday.
Four-time NBA Most Valuable Player James, who turns 42 on December 30, scored a season-high 25 points, passed off a season-high 12 assists and pulled down 10 rebounds for the 76ers.

Miami grabbed a 32-29 lead after the first quarter, but James scored 14 consecutive Sixers points in a second-quarter run for a 62-53 halftime lead, and the hosts never lost the lead in the second half.

stories.title: Sindh High Court restores dissolution of marriage provision in Christian divorce law
summary: KARACHI: The Sindh High Court on Wednesday revived a provision of the Divorce Act of 1869 that had been omitted in 1981, enabling Christian couples in the province to approach courts for dissolution of marriage on ordinary grounds.

Former military dictator Ziaul Haq had omitted Section 7 of the Divorce Act through an ordinance in July 1981, leaving Christian citizens with no ground to divorce their spouses except on charges of adultery.

The bench noted in its judgement that, apparently, the divorce law had recognised cruelty and desertion for two years or more as conduct sufficiently grave to warrant a decree of judicial separation, but not on their own as grounds for dissolution of the marriage.
